svg.title: Hearing loss: the Weber and Rinne together split conductive (ear canal; otitis media; a fixed or broken middle ear) from sensorineural (sudden, an emergency; gradual and symmetric; one-sided and progressive, a vestibular schwannoma until proven otherwise); each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Hearing loss: is sound BLOCKED before the cochlea, or is the cochlea or nerve DAMAGED?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 512 Hz tuning forks, ALWAYS both: Weber on the midline (where is it loudest?) + Rinne (mastoid, then beside the ear)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: a SUDDEN conductive loss can wait; a SUDDEN sensorineural loss is an EMERGENCY

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Weber → the AFFECTED ear · Rinne there: bone > air

svg.text: audiogram: bone normal, air down (an air-bone gap)
